ledger.note: 19 April 1810: Caracas forms its own junta. 'the establishment of the Junta Suprema de Caracas on 19 April 1810', 'The Supreme Junta to Preserve the Rights of Ferdinand VII'; 'The Caracas Junta ... continued to govern Caracas Province'. The page does not list the provinces that followed; the region is Cliopatria's 1811 shape without Coro.

5 July 1811: Venezuela declares independence. 'Independence was formally declared on 5 July 1811' (the infobox says 1810; the text says 1811). The constitution followed on 21 December 1811 ('ratified on 21 December 1811', a bicameral legislature and a triumvirate).

4 July 1812: Barcelona goes royalist. 'an uprising brought Barcelona over to the royalist side'; Cumaná, which refused to recognise Miranda's dictatorial powers, was among the outlying areas that had defected by mid-July. Barcelona is read as the modern state of Anzoátegui.

ledger.note: 25 July 1812: Miranda capitulates. 'On 25 July 1812 Miranda and Monteverde finalized a capitulation' under which former republican areas would recognise the Cortes of Cádiz; Monteverde had taken Valencia by mid-July and entered Caracas on 1 August. Before the capitulation Miranda held 'only a small area of central Venezuela'.

7 August 1813: the Second Republic. The republic was 'declared by Simón Bolívar on 7 August 1813' at the Admirable Campaign (infobox 'Admirable Campaign: 7 August 1813'); the page gives Caracas as capital and no territory.

notes:
ONE STATE OR TWO. Cliopatria's 'Republic of Venezuela' (1811-1814) and 'Venezuela' (1834-2024) share Wikidata Q717 (one item for the country and its first republics), but they are different states for the map: the First and Second Republics fell to the royalists (1812, 1814), Gran Colombia (1819-1830) intervened, and the 1830 republic is a separate polity. This dossier keeps the two republics (First and Second, a 'rename' in 1813) in one colour and does not merge with 'venezuela', which another part writes. The 'venezuela' dossier should list republic-of-venezuela and gran-colombia as predecessors.

SPAN. Cliopatria starts in 1811; the Captaincy General of Venezuela dossier (am-06-x) records its loss to this state in April 1810, so the life starts with the Junta Suprema de Caracas (19 April 1810), with a new 1810 keyframe. It ends on 16 July 1814 (loss of Caracas); the patriot holdouts of 1817-1819 (Piar and Mariño at Angostura and Guayana, the 'Third Republic') are named in that dossier with counterpart 'republic-of-venezuela' for 1817 but have no Cliopatria row and no dossier: a gap-filler should write 'third-republic-of-venezuela' or extend this one.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Which provinces followed the Caracas junta, and which belonged to the Second Republic: neither page says; Cliopatria's shape (minus Coro) is the proxy. (2) The eastern republic of Mariño in 1813 (Cumaná, Margarita) is not on either page. (3) When Valencia became the capital: the infobox only. (4) Both pages give no area; Cliopatria's 400,399 km2 against about 375,000 km2 without Falcón cannot be compared with an infobox figure. (5) Cliopatria's 1811 shape runs to 1813 and so shows the republic alive during 1812-1813, when the royalists held the land from 25 July 1812 to 7 August 1813: the ledger's loss and gain carry that, and the renderer should not hold the 1811 outline through those months.

DISAGREEMENTS. The First Republic infobox dates the Declaration 5 July 1810; the text says 1811. The Second Republic page says the republic 'came to an end in the following year', contradicting the 1813-1814 span of its own infobox; 1814 is used.

GAZETTEER. Every name resolves (Anzoátegui, Falcón, the Cliopatria shape).
